units.function: Four real-database tests specifying destructive Agent and Company removal order across Runs, events, issues, comments, activity, execution decisions, documents/revisions, read state, Skills, Routines and principals.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> agent/company services -> real Drizzle schema on embedded PostgreSQL; no route authorization, storage, Connector or external-system boundary is exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Issue, Run/Event, ActivityLog, IssueExecutionDecision, comment/read state, document/revision, Skill and Routine.
units.lifecycle: Seed a connected company graph -> call service remove directly -> expect dependent operational, collaboration and audit/evidence rows deleted before Agent/Company deletion.
units.testAssessment: Source defines four focused referential-cleanup cases. The 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest run skipped the file and all four tests because embedded PostgreSQL was unavailable; the immediately preceding approved unsandboxed Cases run proved the same host limitation, so no redundant reread/rerun or pass claim is made.
units.designRationale: Explicit deletion order avoids foreign-key failures in a densely connected schema and makes destructive cleanup deterministic.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs lawful offboarding, tenant deletion and right-to-erasure workflows while preserving or pseudonymizing responsibility/evidence under explicit retention, legal-hold and data-owner policy.
units.companyOsFit: REJECT the cascading evidence-deletion semantics. Reimplement a staged RetentionDisposition plan: freeze execution, enumerate data classes, require accountable approval, export/hold where required, revoke credentials, tombstone principals, pseudonymize personal fields, cryptographically erase eligible Secrets/data and record an immutable deletion certificate. Hard delete only after policy gates and recovery windows.
units.responsibilityConflict: The tested contract deletes ActivityLog, Agent-authored comments, issue execution decisions and document revisions—the exact records needed to answer who acted, approved and produced evidence. Company removal therefore erases responsibility instead of closing it with a durable disposition record.
evidence: 2026-08-19 focused Vitest: 1 file/4 tests skipped because embedded PostgreSQL unsupported
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL governance conflict: removal intentionally destroys audit/activity, execution decisions, authored comments and revision history with no tombstone, retention reason, legal hold or deletion certificate. One test inserts a heartbeat event scoped to another company but sharing the deleted run ID and expects it removed, proving run-ID cleanup can cross the event's declared tenant boundary when inconsistent data exists; the schema/service should prevent or quarantine such mismatches rather than normalize them by cross-company deletion. Missing coverage includes authorization/MFA/approval, preview/digest, active-run fencing, concurrent writes, transaction/crash rollback, idempotent retry, storage/blob/Secret/backup/search/log deletion, Connector/external revocation, recovery window and evidence that unrelated tenant rows always survive.
